# exshell

> exshell is a free, open-source (BSD 3-Clause) command-line viewer for CSV, TSV and Excel (.xlsx, .xlsm) files. It is read-only. When its output is piped or redirected it writes plain, aligned, untruncated text, so AI agents and scripts can use it to read tabular data from a shell.

- Homepage: https://vanlabeke.dev/exshell/
- Source: https://github.com/vanlabeke/exshell
- Releases: https://github.com/vanlabeke/exshell/releases
- Agent skill (drop-in SKILL.md): https://vanlabeke.dev/exshell/SKILL.md
- Platforms: macOS (universal, signed and notarized), Linux (amd64, arm64), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD
- Single static binary written in Go, no runtime dependencies

## When an agent should use exshell

Use exshell when you need to read or review the contents of a spreadsheet-like file from a terminal:

- An `.xlsx` or `.xlsm` workbook. Most shells have no other way to read one without Python libraries or LibreOffice.
- A `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.psv` or `.txt` file whose delimiter is comma, semicolon, tab or pipe, including European Excel exports that use `;`.
- A file whose dates, currency or percentages must be read as Excel displays them, not as raw serial numbers (`45291`) or fractions (`0.125`).
- A large CSV where `cat` would produce unaligned output that is hard to reason about.

Do not use exshell to edit, sort, filter, compute or convert data. Pipe its output to `grep`, `head`, `sort` or `awk` for that, or use a data library.

## Check it is installed

```bash
command -v exshell && exshell --version
```

## Install

```bash
# macOS / Linux with Homebrew
brew tap vanlabeke/tap
brew trust --formula vanlabeke/tap/exshell
brew install exshell

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo install -d /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://pkg.vanlabeke.dev/apt/gpg.key | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/vanlabeke.asc > /dev/null
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/vanlabeke.asc] https://pkg.vanlabeke.dev/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/vanlabeke.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install exshell

# Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE
sudo curl -fsSL -o /etc/yum.repos.d/vanlabeke.repo https://pkg.vanlabeke.dev/yum/vanlabeke.repo
sudo dnf install exshell

# From source (Go 1.26+), no sudo
git clone https://github.com/vanlabeke/exshell && cd exshell && make install PREFIX=$HOME/.local
```

Ask the user before installing software on their machine.

## Recommended invocations for agents

Always pass `--print` (`-p`). It guarantees plain-text output and never starts the interactive full-screen viewer, even if the agent's shell happens to be attached to a TTY.

```bash
# Read a whole file
exshell --print data.csv

# Excel: list the sheets first, then read one by name or 1-based index
exshell --list-sheets report.xlsx
exshell --print --sheet Orders report.xlsx
exshell --print --sheet 2 report.xlsx

# Preview a large file, then search it
exshell --print big.csv | head -50
exshell --print big.csv | grep -i "overdue"

# Row count (subtract 2 for the header and the dashed rule line)
exshell --print data.csv | wc -l

# A file without a header row: columns are labelled A, B, C, ...
exshell --print --no-header data.csv

# Unusual input
exshell --print --delim ';' data.txt
exshell --print --encoding latin1 legacy.csv
```

Flags and the file argument may appear in any order.

## Output format

When stdout is not a terminal (or with `--print`):

1. Line 1: the header row (row 1 of the file, unless `--no-header`).
2. Line 2: a rule of dashes under each column.
3. Then one line per data row.

Columns are separated by two spaces. Numeric columns are right-aligned, text columns left-aligned. Trailing whitespace is trimmed. No cell is truncated when output is piped (unless you pass `--max-col-width`, so don't). Embedded newlines and tabs inside a cell are shown as spaces, so one output line is always one row.

Example:

```
Order Date  Product    Price  Discount
----------  -------  -------  --------
01-15-26    Widget    $19.99       10%
02-03-26    Gadget   $249.50        0%
```

For `.xlsx`, values are the format-applied values Excel would display: dates in the cell's own date format, currency with its symbol, percentages as percentages. Formulas show their cached result, not the formula.

## Flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-p`, `--print` | force plain-text output, even to a terminal |
| `-i`, `--interactive` | force the interactive viewer (not useful for agents) |
| `--sheet <name\|#>` | sheet to open, by name or 1-based index |
| `--list-sheets` | print sheet names, one per line, and exit |
| `--delim <char>` | override the sniffed CSV delimiter |
| `--no-header` | treat row 1 as data; label columns A, B, C, ... |
| `--encoding <enc>` | input encoding: `utf8`, `latin1` or `utf16` |
| `--max-col-width <n>` | cap column width, truncating with `…` |
| `--version` | print the version and exit |
| `-h`, `--help` | print usage and exit |

## Exit codes and errors

- `0`: success.
- `1`: runtime error, such as a missing or unreadable file, a password-protected `.xlsx`, or a legacy `.xls` file.
- `2`: usage error, such as an unknown flag or a `--sheet` that does not exist.

Errors are written to stderr as one line prefixed with `exshell:`. stdout is empty on error.

## Limitations

- Read-only viewer: no editing, formulas, sorting or filtering.
- The whole file is loaded into memory. Fine for typical exports, not for multi-gigabyte files.
- Input must be a file path. Reading from stdin is not supported.
- Legacy `.xls` and password-protected workbooks are not supported. Ask the user to re-save as `.xlsx`.
- Merged cells: the value appears only in the merge's top-left cell; the other cells are empty.
- Row 1 is always the header unless `--no-header` is given. There is no header detection.
- Only trailing empty rows and columns are trimmed. Blank rows inside the data are kept.
- Hidden sheets are included in `--list-sheets` and can be opened with `--sheet`.
